open_obligations: Check that 'approximate global equilibrium' in Buhl et al. matches A-leading Stackelberg equilibria.
Check that the safety case accounts for the stability and A-provability conditions.
Note the guarantee is average-case over inputs.

Theorem 6.2 is a formal result about the prover-estimator debate protocol, while claim 2 is about the system in the safety case; check that this system and its debate game fit the theorem's model, not only its equilibrium notion and hypotheses.

Buhl et al. call prover-estimator debate forthcoming and say their argument structure should apply to other protocols; check that claim 2 is meant to rest on this protocol's Theorem 6.2 and not only on some protocol with honest equilibria.
out.other_title: Theorem 6.2: correct answers at Stackelberg equilibria (prob. 1 - 5 eps)
out.rationale: Buhl et al.'s key claim 2 is that in approximate global equilibria the system errs on at most an eps'-fraction of cases. They require a debate protocol in whose global equilibrium both debaters are honest, and say they wrote the sketch with prover-estimator debate (forthcoming) in mind, though the argument structure should apply to other protocols. Brown-Cohen et al. state that debaters can be trained in prover-estimator debate via standard methods that converge to Stackelberg equilibria in zero-sum games, and that, given rho-stability and A-provability, Theorem 6.2 implies A will produce the correct answer with probability at least 1 - 5 eps, which is the kind of result claim 2 needs.
out.scope: proposed DEPENDS_ON: the safety case's claim that approximate equilibria of the debate game imply a bounded error rate, in a sketch written with prover-estimator debate in mind

text: The authors list four key claims a developer must defend: (1) training has reached an approximate global equilibrium of the debate game; (2) in approximate global equilibria the system makes mistakes in at most an eps'-fraction of cases; (3) during deployment, with online training, the error rate will not drift past eps; and (4) the system cannot cause unacceptable outcomes given an error rate of eps.
title: Four key claims of the debate safety case: equilibrium, error bound, no drift, low stakes
